lines.text: A land of lakes and forests, ruled by Sweden and then Russia, that found its voice in song and fought hard to stay free. This is Finland.
For about six centuries, from the Middle Ages, Finland was part of the Swedish realm.
Its first city grew on the south-west coast. Turku is the oldest town in Finland, and was long its capital.
In 1550 a Swedish king founded Helsinki on the southern shore, a small town then, the capital today.
In 1809 Russia took Finland from Sweden. As a grand duchy under the tsars, it kept its own laws.
Elias Lonnrot travelled the countryside gathering old folk songs, and wove them into the Kalevala, the national epic.
In 1865 a paper mill was set up beside a river. Its name was Nokia, and one day it would make phones for the world.
The same year Jean Sibelius was born. His Finlandia and seven symphonies would give the nation its music.
Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim would one day lead Finland's armies, and later become its president.
Paavo Nurmi, the Flying Finn, would win nine Olympic gold medals and put his country on the sporting map.
Urho Kekkonen would be president for twenty-six years, keeping Finland free through careful dealings with Moscow.
And Tove Jansson would create the Moomins, gentle creatures loved by children around the world.
As Russia fell into revolution, Finland seized its moment. On the sixth of December 1917, it declared independence.
After centuries under others, Finland stood as a nation of its own.
But freedom began in bloodshed. In 1918 Reds and Whites fought a short and bitter civil war.
In 1939 the Soviet Union invaded. Through a freezing winter, the Finns held off a far larger army.
Two years later fighting with the Soviets broke out again, and lasted until 1944.
In 1952 Helsinki welcomed the world to the Olympic Games, and Emil Zatopek ran into legend.
Alexander Stubb, born in 1968, would become president in 2024.
In 1975, thirty-five states of East and West met in Helsinki and promised to respect borders and human rights.
In 1991 a Helsinki student, Linus Torvalds, started a hobby project. Linux now runs most of the world's servers.
In 2003 the game studio Rovio was founded. Its Angry Birds would be played on phones everywhere.
Since 2018 a yearly world report has named Finland the happiest country on Earth, again and again.
And after Russia invaded Ukraine, Finland left its long neutrality behind and joined NATO in 2023.
From folk songs to phones and NATO, Finland has kept its quiet, stubborn independence.
